c74object.name: ossia.client
c74object.digest: Connect to a distant Ossia device
c74object.description: ossia.client allows to connect to a distant device (either locally or on another computer) through various protocols, and lets you bind to it through ossia.view and ossia.remote

outlet.name: Info outlet
outlet.description: Messages and information in reply to various messages. connect followed by 1 and the connection parameters when the device is connected, by 0 when the connection failed or when the server went away, for a connection by URL or by name; the object then tries again every second (see reconnect) and sends connect 1 again when the server is back. By URL: connect 1 or 0, then the connection parameters (oscquery, a name, the URL). By name: connect 1 or 0, then the name. disconnected when a device connected by name goes away. devices followed by their number, then one device line per device found, in reply to get devices.

method.name: namespace
method.digest: Output list of all parameters and their current values
method.description: Sending the namespace message to the leftmost inlet outputs the list of all parameters registered under this node, and their current values

method.name: get
method.digest: Get the list of all discoverable devices on the network
method.description: The message get devices outputs on the outlet devices followed by the number of devices found on the network (Minuit and OSCQuery), then a line per device with its protocol and its name. get followed by another attribute name outputs that attribute, as for ossia.device.

method.name: connect
method.digest: Connect to a global device to the network
method.description:
The connect message to the leftmost inlet will print its configuration parameters for the various available protocols Then, sending it with the appropriate values will connect to the appropriate device on the network, and allow it to be explored, queried and remotely-controlled. Notice that, if the get devices message has not been sent previously, the object will internally do it, which might take some time, and delay the actual connection accordingly. With connect oscquery <url>, the connection runs on a thread of its own, so that Max does not wait for the server, which may be an ossia.device of the same Max; the outlet sends connect 1 when the device is connected and its tree read. The object then follows the server's WebSocket: when it goes down (the server stopped), the outlet sends connect 0 with the connection parameters, and every second the object tries again, as long as reconnect is on, until the server answers; it then reads the tree again and subscribes again to every parameter it follows, and the outlet sends connect 1. A disconnect or a new connect stops the attempts.
With connect <name>, the object connects to the OSCQuery device announced over mDNS (_oscjson._tcp) under that name, on this machine, the same Max included, or another one of the same network. Until the device is found, the outlet sends connect 0 <name> and the object tries again every second. Once connected, when the device's WebSocket goes down while it is still announced (its server stopped, or its application quit abruptly), the outlet sends disconnected then connect 0 <name> within about a second; when the device is no longer announced, the outlet sends disconnected. In both cases the object tries again every second while reconnect is on, and sends connect 1 <name> when the device is back. The message get devices lists the devices found, those whose tree is read. Create the object without argument, then send it connect <name>. Created with a name only (ossia.client <name>), the object sends itself connect without argument as it is created: every second, the outlet sends connect with nothing after it and the console prints the help of the protocols, until a connect with arguments or a disconnect. Followed by a float, the name is not connected at creation when the float is 0.; followed by an integer, the object connects by name to that name. Connected by name, the object reads the device's tree again: the outlet sends parameter removed and node removed for every node, then node created and parameter created, and the ossia.remote objects register again.

method.name: disconnect
method.digest: Disconnect from the currently connected remoted device
method.description: The disconnect message to the leftmost inlet will disconnect ossia.client from the currently remoted device

method.name: update
method.digest: Update the namespace of the remote device
method.description: For some protocols or remote devices, the remote namespace is not automatically updated. Sending the "update" message will do this.

method.name: preset
method.description: Sending the preset save /path/to/file.txt message to the leftmost inlet will write a list of all parameters and their values to the the disk, under the file /path/to/file.txt Sending the preset load /path/to/file.txt message to the leftmost inlet will load a list of all parameters and their values from the the file /path/to/file.txt, and recall the values to the parameters

method.name: set
method.description: The set message followed by a distant node address and value will set the node to the value specified as argument

attribute.name: description
attribute.description: The description attribute allows to give a textual description for this node. This helps documenting the parameter.

attribute.name: invisible
attribute.description: The invisible attribute allows to hide device on the network. Note that this attribute cannot be changed once the device has been exposed on the network

attribute.name: priority
attribute.description: The priority attribute allows to order how several values of a same hierarchical level can be recalled

attribute.name: bundle
attribute.digest: Send the values of a tick in OSC bundles
attribute.description: The bundle attribute groups what the objects of this device (ossia.parameter, ossia.remote, ossia.view) push during a tick of the scheduler: the values leave at the end of the tick, in OSC bundles of at most 1400 bytes over UDP, in order, nothing merged (two values of one address both leave). -1 (default): bundles when the device speaks OSCQuery; 0: one message per value; 1: always. ossia.v8connector groups its own values (its bundle attribute).

attribute.name: reconnect
attribute.digest: Reconnect when the server goes away
attribute.description: The reconnect attribute (default: on) makes a client connected by URL (connect oscquery <url>) or by name (connect <name>) try again every second when the server's WebSocket goes down, or, by name, when the device is no longer announced, until the server answers. Off, the loss is reported on the outlet and nothing is tried. The attribute governs only the attempts after a loss: a first connection that fails (an unreachable URL, a name not found) is tried again every second whatever reconnect says, until it succeeds, a disconnect or a new connect.

attribute.name: recall_safe
attribute.digest: Enable or disable value update when recalling preset
attribute.description: The recall_safe attribute (default: off) allows to prevent value update when recalling a preset. This can be handy for example in live situation to prevent a model or parameter state to be recalled while being controlled by some processes (manual control, mapping, etc.)

attribute.name: tags
attribute.description: The tags attribute allows to associate a variable number of tags for this node. This helps documenting the parameter.

attribute.name: trim_address
attribute.digest: Output absolute or relative address path
attribute.description: The trim_address attribute sets whether the address is output as a relative or absolute path
